slot.brief: Alkyl halide + Mg in dry ether followed by reaction with a carbonyl and hydrolysis — identify the final alcohol product.

stem: Ethyl bromide reacts with magnesium in dry ether, followed by propanone and hydrolysis. What is the final alcohol?

verdicts.working: Ethyl bromide forms ethylmagnesium bromide, which adds an ethyl group to propanone. Hydrolysis gives (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃, 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

working:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}+\text{Mg}\rightarrow\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$; $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}+(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CO}\rightarrow(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{OMgBr})\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$; hydrolysis gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}(\text{OH})\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ = 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

Independent check: Ethyl bromide forms ethylmagnesium bromide, which adds an ethyl group to propanone. Hydrolysis gives (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃, 2-methylbutan-2-ol.
solution:
Ethyl bromide forms the Grignard reagent, which adds to propanone; hydrolysis gives a tertiary alcohol.
$$\mathrm{C_2H_5MgBr+(CH_3)_2CO\xrightarrow{H_3O^+}(CH_3)_2C(OH)C_2H_5}$$
The product is 2-methylbutan-2-ol.
